pre_fix_attack_run_fair_seed_101.note: raw run folder deleted by mistake; numbers from the console scorecard

limitations: Under the 10k-client real-backend run, only 121/200 genuine users entered in the Fair run, so full genuine-user availability under this attack load is not yet proven. This is an availability/capacity limitation, not evidence that the fairness mechanism failed.

All 79 genuine users who did not enter never completed OTP sign-in after their retries (the 5xx in the pre-fix run were 503 on /auth/otp/request and /auth/otp/verify); every genuine user who signed in entered exactly once. The remaining cause is not isolated yet; the per-route 5xx breakdown was not captured for this run.
One post-fix seed only (101); the planned 3-seed run was not done.
Bot rejection rate is request-level (429s), not the share of bots kept from seats.
Fair mode does not remove the identity-count (Sybil) advantage; it removes the speed/request-volume advantage and limits each verified identity to one entry.
Farm detection: 0 farm entries reached the step-up score in this run (L6 kept farm accounts at <= 3 per device, below the R_DEVICE threshold).
Cloud sandbox: Docker started manually, local image shims for the proxy CA and dbmate, nofile capped at 20000 (none committed).
